THERAVĀDA I — PASS C2-B5
RŪPĀRŪPAVIBHĀGA — FINAL CRITICAL APPARATUS v1

PURPOSE
This apparatus accompanies a diplomatic PTS-based text.
It does not claim to constitute a new critical edition.

SIGLA / CONTROLS
PTS  = A. P. Buddhadatta (ed.), Buddhadatta's Manuals I, PTS 1915, pp.149–159.
UPT  = UPT589_4F, Myanmar-script manuscript, fols.249b–254a.
FRY  = Mirko Fryba, modern Roman-Pāli control derived from the PTS publication line.
EXE  = R.H.B. Exell, translation based on PTS 1915.
CM   = A Comprehensive Manual of Abhidhamma (Bhikkhu Bodhi et al.):
       doctrinal/classical-tradition control only; NOT a witness to Rūpārūpavibhāga.
LIRI = LIRI-FPL 6889, complete Burmese witness (catalogue-level control only).

EDITORIAL PRINCIPLE
The PTS 1915 reading is the base. Editorial doubts are preserved.
No conjectural emendation is adopted merely because a doctrinal parallel
would yield smoother Pāli.

A — PTS 149, opening prose
MAIN PTS: Rūpārūpavibhāgan
PTS FOOTNOTE: Rūpārūpavibhāgataṃ (?)
STATUS: main-text reading retained diplomatically.

B — PTS 149
PTS: ādito (paṭṭhāya ?) catubbidhaṃ rūpaṃ
STATUS: uncertainty preserved in diplomatic text.

C — PTS 150
PTS MAIN: Sakammajarūpaṃ
PTS NOTE: kammajarūpaṃ (?)
STATUS: main PTS reading retained.

D — PTS 150
PTS MAIN: na kehici samuṭṭhahanti
PTS NOTE: na kehici (?)
CLASSICAL/DOCTRINAL CONTROL:
Later Abhidhamma manual tradition contains closely corresponding wording
with kehici in the discussion of the characteristics of matter.
STATUS: PTS main wording retained; no manuscript emendation claimed.

E — PTS 150 — CRITICAL LOCUS
PTS:
Upacaya-santatiyo (catūhi ?) jāyantīti vuccanti.
TEXTUAL STATUS:
UNRESOLVED. The parenthetical catūhi is explicitly doubtful in PTS.
FRY omits it in the running Pāli text; EXE's translation accepts the semantic
force of four causes.
DOCTRINAL CONTROL:
The later Abhidhamma manual tradition distinguishes the four modes of origin
of material phenomena from the status of the characteristics of matter.
This makes a four-cause interpretation intelligible at the level of the material
process, but it does NOT establish catūhi as the original wording here.
EDITORIAL DECISION:
PRESERVE EXACTLY AS PTS. No insertion, deletion, or emendation.

F — PTS 150
PTS MAIN: rūpavikāro
PTS NOTE: rūpaṃ vikāro
STATUS: main PTS reading retained.

G — PTS 150
PTS MAIN: lakkhaṇarūpāni
PTS NOTE: lakkhaṇarūpaṃ (?)
STATUS: main PTS reading retained.

H — PTS 150 — VERY HIGH-RISK LOCUS
PTS:
(Na arūpakasattānaṃ paṭisandhikāle na saddo viyāti (?).
TEXTUAL STATUS:
UNRESOLVED; probably corrupt, contaminated, or gloss-like is an editorial
diagnosis/inference, NOT an established manuscript reading.
DOCTRINAL CONTROL:
The later Abhidhamma manual tradition separately states:
(1) no materiality occurs in the immaterial realm; and
(2) sound is absent at the initial arising/rebirth-linking stage.
The PTS clause appears to combine these two doctrinal environments, which
helps explain its difficulty but does not authorize a conjectural correction.
EDITORIAL DECISION:
RETAIN THE PTS CLAUSE VERBATIM IN THE DIPLOMATIC LAYER.
NO CONJECTURAL EMENDATION ADOPTED.

I — PTS 154
PTS: Hadayaṃ anissāya (?)
STATUS:
PTS uncertainty preserved diplomatically. Later Abhidhamma manual tradition
strongly supports the doctrinal content, but no silent correction is made.

MANUSCRIPT CONTROL
UPT589_4F:
- identity: Rūpārūpavibhāga
- continuous supplied sequence: 249b–254a
- role: independent manuscript witness
- word-level E/H readings: NOT CLAIMED in this apparatus

ATTRIBUTION
Conventional/PTS attribution: Buddhadatta.
Some catalogue/traditional evidence attributes the work to Vācissara.
STATUS: DISPUTED; disagreement must be preserved in TH1 metadata.

FINAL C2-B5 DECISION
A diplomatic PTS-based text is fit for TH1 ingestion PROVIDED:
- E and H remain explicitly unresolved;
- H is not conjecturally rewritten;
- UPT589_4F is cited only as manuscript control, not falsely transcribed;
- modern copyrighted control works are not copied into the public repository.
